$schema-note: The canonical copy of this file lives at MetaGer/metager/tests/Fixtures/locale-cases.json and is described by MetaGer/docs/locale-contract.md. It is copied verbatim into app-en, metager-keymanager and SafeBrowse. Change it there first, then copy; a repo whose copy has drifted is a repo whose answer to 'what language is this user' has drifted.

resolution.name: an explicit ?lang= outranks everything else
resolution.why: A client that states its locale is not guessing, and nothing a browser carries should overrule it.

resolution.name: the MG-Locale header says the same thing for a client that cannot use a query string
resolution.why: The WebExtension and the app keep their settings themselves and replay them as headers.

resolution.name: the path prefix outranks the stored locale
resolution.why: A locale-prefixed URL is a link someone followed or typed; the cookie is what they last chose here.

resolution.name: the stored locale outranks the browser's preference
resolution.why: Choosing a language on the site has to survive a browser that never stopped asking for German.

resolution.name: the old setting is read as a language while the new cookie is absent
resolution.why: web_setting_m was the interface language until this contract; a returning browser must not lose its choice.

resolution.name: changing the result market does not move the interface
resolution.why: The whole point of the split: web_setting_m is a search filter again, and only mg_locale says what to render in.

resolution.name: an English browser on the German domain is believed
resolution.why: The rule this contract exists to delete. metager.de used to force German here, and metager.org used to bounce a German browser away.

resolution.name: a German browser on the other domain is believed too
resolution.why: The same rule, in the direction that used to produce a cross-origin redirect and lose the user's key.

resolution.name: every language we ship is negotiable, not just German, English and Spanish
resolution.why: The old Accept-Language table listed three languages, so a French browser matched nothing and got the host default.

resolution.name: Catalan is negotiable like any other language we ship
resolution.why: ca-ES is a supported locale and an offered market; a Catalan browser should not land in Spanish by way of the q=0.8 fallback.

resolution.name: a Catalan path prefix resolves to Catalan
resolution.why: Every supported locale is reachable by URL, whether or not the implementation ships a translation for it.

resolution.name: a bare language gets its home region
resolution.why: Accept-Language is allowed to name a language without a region; the market and the URL both need the full tag.

resolution.name: the German domain is the German fallback
resolution.why: The last remaining use of the host, and the only one: a request that says nothing at all still has to be answered in something.

resolution.name: every other domain falls back to English
resolution.why: The other half of the same rule.

resolution.name: a language we do not ship falls through to the host fallback
resolution.why: Reaching the fallback is not an error and never causes a redirect — it is the answer for a request that named nothing we have.

home_regions.$comment: The region a bare language stands for. MetaGer's LocaleContext::HOME_REGION, app-en's HOME_MARKET keys. Catalan's home region is Spain even though Catalan is also spoken in Andorra and France: ca_ES is the only Catalan market MetaGer offers.

device_markets.$comment: Device locale -> the market a client asks for, or null when the device names nothing we have. Read from the device alone: the interface language plays no part, so a de-AT phone searches Austria whichever language it renders in. Consumed by app-en; MetaGer asserts every non-null value is an offered market in config/filters.json. A region is only used directly when it is one of the locales laravellocalization.php supports AND is not pinned as unsearchable in MarketFilterTest::UNSEARCHABLE_LOCALES — otherwise the language's home region is used instead.
